correctness.rationale: For the real norm whose unit ball has twelve facet inequalities f_j(x)<=1, the definition reduces delta_a(epsilon)=1-M(epsilon)^2/2 where M=max ||x+y|| over unit pairs at separation epsilon. Choose signed supporting facets p for x+y and q for x-y; exact dual vertex support gives ||p±sqrt3 q||_* sums <=4 and ||sqrt3 p±q||_* sums <=4 for all 144 ordered facet pairs. Consequently M<=min{2,4-sqrt3 epsilon,(4-epsilon)/sqrt3}. Independent exact Q(sqrt3) arithmetic reconstructed all twelve vertices, computed seven dihedral facet-separation classes [2sqrt3,2+sqrt3,4,4,4,2+sqrt3,2sqrt3], and verified the upper bounds. It separately proved, by affine endpoint inequalities and identically active facets, that all five explicit families actually have unit coordinates, separation epsilon, and the stated maximal sum on their full intervals [0,a],[a,1],[1,b],[b,sqrt3],[sqrt3,2], with a=4-2sqrt3 and b=2(sqrt3-1). Hence the all-real-epsilon piecewise profile follows analytically, not by finite sampling. Both endpoints epsilon=0 and 2 included.
residual_risks: The bound is confined to the stated normalized regular dodecagonal real plane; no general regular 2n-gon formula.
The computation validates explicit maximizers and exact values, not classification of all maximizing unit pairs.
The proof relies on the unit-ball support model; the 12-vertex exhaustive check covers all its signed facets.

value.rationale: The fixed-separation Clarkson/angle convexity modulus is a canonical quantitative invariant of Banach-space geometry. The regular dodecagon is a natural 12-facet symmetric polyhedral normed plane: its complete continuum profile has a nontrivial plateau 0<=epsilon<=4-2sqrt3 and two subsequent distinct active-facet phases meeting at 2(sqrt3-1). Unlike a one-point norm constant or arbitrary numerical slice, the result supplies a complete natural function, exact transitions and a reusable weighted-dual-facet proof. A researcher comparing uniform convexity failure, polygonal convexity moduli or primal-dual geometric inequalities could need these precise phase boundaries. No general theorem or paper-sized contribution is claimed or needed.
residual_risks: The result is specific to one canonical polygon, not a classification of every polygonal norm.
A generic linear-program algorithm could evaluate any fixed polygon, but the closed continuum phase structure is not just a known table lookup.

final_claim: For all real epsilon in [0,2], M(epsilon)=max{N12(x+y):N12(x)=N12(y)=1,N12(x-y)=epsilon}=min{2,(4-epsilon)/sqrt3,4-sqrt3 epsilon}; angle modulus delta_a_X12(epsilon)=1-M(epsilon)^2/2 with branch transitions 4-2sqrt3 and 2(sqrt3-1).
limitations: Real 2D regular dodecagonal norm only, epsilon in [0,2], no other polygons.
No classification of all maximizing pairs and no stability result.
Best-of-knowledge originality; older unindexed classical modulus equivalent remains possible.
Publisher full text direct open was rate-limited; inspected accessible extracts only, with explicit residual risk.
